text: You see, you love fear. The ending of fear is death, and you don't want THAT to happen.
note: Aggregators continue: 'I am not talking of wiping out the phobias of the body...'; the death of fear is the only death.

text: The body cannot be afraid of death. The movement that is created by society or culture is what does not want to come to an end.
note: Goodreads attributes the same passage both to Mind Is a Myth and to No Way Out.

text: It is fear that makes you believe that you are living and that you will be dead. What we do not want is the fear to come to an end.
note: Only the opening clause is confirmed verbatim ('It is fear that makes you believe that you are living and that you will be dead'); one aggregator cites Mystique p.83. Wording variants 'new science'/'new sciences' reported.

text: What is morality? It is not the following of enjoined rules of conduct.
note: Passage continues on questioning action before and after creating the moral problem; one blog version omits the line about the faculty of distinguishing right from wrong.

text: …the beyond can never be experienced by you; it is when the 'you' is not there.
note: Goodreads carries the related question: why try to experience something that cannot be experienced?

text: The 'you' is born out of fear; it lives in fear, functions in fear and dies in fear.
There is no death for the body; there is only an exchange of atoms.
note: Search summary paraphrase of a Goodreads body-and-death passage attributed to Mind Is a Myth.

text: WHAT I HAVE FOUND, OFF AND BY MYSELF, IS THAT ALL TEACHERS RELIGIOUS, SECULAR AND THOSE SCIENTISTS AND FILTHY DOCTORS ARE WRONG
note: Opening of the Swan Song as given in the WELL page title (page title truncated at 'WRON'). Dictated to Louis Brawley mid-February 2007.

text: It [thought] is a mechanical thing and can solve only mechanical problems. But you want to use it to understand something living…
book: Stopped in Our Tracks, Book Two
note: Compiled by K. Chandrasekhar from tapes, translated from Telugu and edited by J.S.R.L. Narayana Moorty.

text: Thinking is a poor alternative to acting.
note: Wikiquote attributes this and 'Act, don't think!' to Mahesh Bhatt's book (Wikiquote labels it 'A Taste of Death', 1995) and warns Bhatt's framing has been misquoted as part of UG's own statement.

text: Act, don't think!
note: Via Mahesh Bhatt; see Wikiquote caveat on misquotation.

text: Everything you stand for, believe in, experience and aspire to is the result of thought. And thought is destructive…
Life has to be described in pure and simple physical and physiological terms.
The death of fear is the only death.
note: Closing line of the 'You love fear' passage.

text: All your experiences, all your meditations, all your prayer, all that you do, is self-centred. … whatever you do to be free from the self also is a self-centred activity … strengthening the self, adding momentum, gathering momentum, so it is taking you in the opposite direction.
note: Stitched from two search renderings of azquotes 765776.

text: This state is a state of not knowing.
note: Opening line of the Wikisource compilation 'The Natural State'.

text: There is no meaning in and no purpose to suffering.
Sex is for reproduction; people have turned it into a pleasure pursuit. An enlightened man cannot have sex because he cannot reproduce another like himself.
note: Paraphrase from search summaries of the Swan Song text.

text: If the body lacks the means to survive it goes gracefully.
note: Paraphrase; the Swan Song also speaks of the body's self-regulating intelligence.

text: There is nothing there - no soul - there is only this question about after death.
note: From a quote-collection page; book not identified.

text: What is there is only the body. It is actually a computer, but we are not ready to accept it.
note: Two adjacent fragments from the transcript opening as rendered by the search summary.

text: "An ashram-like atmosphere can't grow around me," roared U.G. … "Neither my tapes nor books nor letters must be in anyone's control."
note: Reported speech in Chandrasekhar's journal, 1972 Bangalore period.

text: Love implies division, separation. Wherever there is division, there can't be love.
note: Goodreads work 43411143 is titled after this quote.

text: We are trying to bridge this gap… with this fancy idea that there must be love between these two individuals.
Thought always interferes with sex. It has become a pleasure movement.
The pleasure of sex, for instance, is by nature temporary. The body can't take uninterrupted pleasure for long, it would be destroyed.
By giving money they control you, and by not giving money they control you.
note: Inner-quest 'UG Words' collection; UG adds that the only test for him is how free a person is with money.

text: The only relationship you have with anybody in this world is "What do I get out of it?"
There is nothing to your love: if you don't get what you want, what happens to your, "I love you darling…"
I have wasted seven years listening to you.
note: Paraphrase of UG's break with J. Krishnamurti c.1953 as told in Mahesh Bhatt's biography.

text: The whole thing comes to an end.
note: Reality Sandwich excerpt from Mukunda Rao's compilation of 1967-71 conversations.

text: …this is the way you, stripped of the machinations of thought, are also functioning.
note: Quoted in the book synopsis as a line UG 'never tires of pointing out'.

text: Can you give me what you have?
note: UG's question to Ramana Maharshi; Ramana's reply 'I can give you, but can you take it?' UG called his seven years with Sivananda 'a useless exercise' (secondary account).

text: Yoga, meditation and prayer are violent techniques. The living body is very peaceful; you don't have to do a thing.
note: Quoted via Mark Whitwell / Heart of Yoga; Whitwell's Medium essay also carries the fragment 'Meditation is evil'.

text: Man has created God out of fear. So the problem is fear and not God.
note: Continuation of the already-harvested 'There is no power outside of man'.

text: …all the positive approaches that man has invented and used for centuries have not resulted in anything useful. They have not produced the results you have been promised.
Charity is the filthiest invention of the human mind: first… [people give charity to prevent the have-nots from rebelling, and it also makes them feel less guilty].
note: Opening clause verbatim; bracketed continuation is a summary rendering. A blog also lists 'Charity is selfishness.'

text: The belief in reincarnation will only help us to look the other side.
You have to liberate yourself.
We are not created for any grander purpose than the ants that are there or the flies that are hovering around you or the mosquitoes that are sucking your blood.
note: Wikisource ch.4 wording ('you'); aggregators give 'We are not created… than the ants… the flies… the mosquitoes' in third person. Supersedes the fragment entry above.

text: Each cell of a living organism cooperates with the cell next to it. … The cells stick together not out of brotherhood, love and that kind of thing, but out of the urgent drive to survive.
book: Society: It's terror, not love that keeps us together
note: Sunita Pant Bansal (ed.), foreword Mahesh Bhatt; passage closes with a line about destroying a neighbour. Goodreads work 45622919.

text: It is not love, compassion, humanism, or brotherly sentiments that will save mankind. It is the sheer terror of extinction that can save us, if anything can.
note: The Mind Is a Myth introduction samples the same idea as 'mutual terror, not love, will save mankind'; the Bansal anthology title renders it 'It's terror, not love that keeps us together'.

text: Our basic human problems are neurological, not psychological. Thought has created the problem of desire.
book: Certainty: Life has no beginning, no end
note: Search-summary paraphrase of Goodreads work 46398939 (Bansal anthology 'Certainty'); same page: drop the idea of the meaningful and you find meaning in daily life.

text: I have nothing to say and what I am saying is not born out of my thinking.
note: Transcribed conversation reproduced in Mahesh Bhatt's biography (blog serialisation); no date or venue given, so not confirmed as the 1972 Bangalore 'First and Last Public Talk'.

text: India will *not* be that country.
note: UG predicts the world crisis will produce its rescue from the West, grounding it in having spent half his life in the West.

text: …anything you superimpose on that, all the cultural input, is responsible for the boredom of man.
note: Quotepark 'Culture' tag; same page paraphrases 'as a human being I am rotten because of the culture'.

text: You draw lines on this planet.
note: Context: thought creates the world and its borders, so unity between countries is unreachable.

text: Hope is necessary for tomorrow, not for today.
note: Goodreads attribution; page formatting messy.

text: The peace you seek is already there; the effort to be at peace is what destroys it.
note: Paraphrase of the libquotes 'peace' topic passage.

text: Human nature is basically violent because thought itself is violent.
note: Hindu-blog collection; same page says the body dissolves into its elements at death and in that sense is immortal.

text: I have never taken any medicine or seen a doctor, except once for typhoid. I would never tell others not to see a doctor, though I say doctors should be shot.
note: Paraphrase from the Medium/WELL copies of the Swan Song.

text: I have one thing against medical technology…
note: Dated 1982 on quotewise/quotepark; continues about controlling the human being.

text: The body knows what it needs to survive; if it lacks the means it goes gracefully.
note: Recurs in inner-quest 'UG Words', hindu-blog and the Swan Song.

text: You need not worry about nutrition or health foods; the body turns whatever you put into it into energy.
note: Interview account in the 'UG Cookbook' PDF (travelswithug.com), at age 84; not verbatim.

text: …I knew without doubt that I had made the biggest mistake of my life.
note: On the morning after his arranged wedding; the same source reports he did not trust anyone who had not raised children to educate them ('if you raised your own children, you would understand').

text: If you could have sex with your own mother without any psychological or spiritual problem, that would be the end of your sexual desire.
note: Paraphrase of a Wikisource ch.8 dialogue; same passage: 'Thought always interferes with sex.'

text: There is no such thing as your mind and my mind. … mind is everywhere, sort of like the air we breathe.
There is no such thing as spiritual or psychological enlightenment because there is no such thing as spirit or psyche.
note: Wikiquote dates the book 1987.

text: People call me enlightened, a term I dislike; there is no such thing as enlightenment.
note: Summary paraphrase of a Wikiquote Mystique entry.

text: Charity is selfishness.
note: Blog list of sayings, source unclear.

text: Meditation is evil.
note: Fragment in Mark Whitwell's Medium essay; surrounding context cut off.
